Date: 2026-10-02. Reviewer: independent adversarial pass, Opus. Scope: entries whose `chapter:` is one of npgdKKdJSww, AgouMNTeyo4, 40NV3_u9tYY, BJkCqf6Fj2w, J7smyg1Czik, sHXuxj3-rbQ, QLdbKUiNadg, TbYgc6_qQzo, EeBgUCYhezc, SIn6IyYQEVI, TIRINmtZOu0, z_6M5r7031A. The other 11 talks belong to reviewer r4b.

**Summary: 80 entries. GO 35, FIX 45, NO-GO 0. 56% needed changes.** Every FIX was applied in the entry file as a minimal, bounded edit. No file was deleted, nothing was committed or promoted, and the vault was not touched.

## Method

1. A mechanical pass over all 80 entries checked the following: the frontmatter keys and their order against the brief (with the extra `source` key), the kind prefix, the quoted `chapter`, `created`, the six `**X** —` headers, em dashes in body text, review-history phrases, and that every `<id> [mm:ss]` locator is a real marker inside that transcript's range. Every `[[wikilink]]` was resolved against the book folder and the SecondBrain library. **Result: all 80 entries pass, and all 37 vault links resolve.** The pass was re-run after the fixes, with no regressions.
2. Each entry was then read against the transcript windows it cites, with summary.md used only to cross-check. The checks were:
   - Claims, numbers and quotes appear in the caption text at the cited block or the block next to it.
   - Confidence follows this rule: `supported` needs both a method and a result the speaker reports. Assertions, second-hand uncited studies and procedures with no outcome are `untested`.
   - Named people are spoken aloud in the captions or appear in the title.
   - Pronouns appear in the captions.
   - Every "Eric's baseline:" line is traceable to `docs/method-baseline.md` and carries its tag.
   - Unlabelled mechanisms and examples are flagged.
   - Duplicates within the book are flagged.
3. Cross-talk duplicate pairs were compared directly: velocity and elbow stress vs throwing harder; the two fatigue entries; the two return-after-surgery entries; the three youth entries; keep-the-load vs adjust-the-model; and the three ACWR schedule entries. None is a near-duplicate. Each pair takes a different angle or a different dataset, and most already cross-link.

# AGENTS.md

Project: Flint

## What this is
Flint is Claude working as Eric's sport-science, performance, S&C and rehab thought
partner. This repo builds the knowledge base behind that role. It catalogs Eric's
Drive (his own material, TB's Training Info, Landon Evans, courses, papers), routes the
high-value sources into Zotero and the SecondBrain vault, and writes per-discipline
synthesis notes that compare the sources against Eric's own method. It is a side-lane
project, outside the prioritization-slate cap. See `README.md` for the approach and
`docs/PLAN.md` for the checklist.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- `data/` is gitignored except aggregate summaries. Regenerate the file-level manifest with `pwsh scripts/build_manifest.ps1`.
- Codex workers read staged copies in `staging/`, never the Drive root. DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued.
- The ingest review gate has two stages.
  1. Before atomizing, verify the source artifact by an independent route: page order, scanned versus text, transcripts checked against captions.
  2. Before promoting, Codex reviews the staged entries against the staged sources, with instructions to falsify (`staging/review_<source>_codex.md`). Nothing reaches the vault without a GO or a GO AFTER FIXES that has been applied.
- Library entries label every voice. The source author's statements are plain. Eric's judgments get "Eric's review:". The entry writer's own reasoning gets "Inference:". No unlabeled judgments. Every number carries a timestamp or page the reviewer can check, and a claim is only tagged "confirmed in PDF" if that PDF is staged. (Learned from the Harries review, 2026-09-26: 25 of 35 files needed fixes, mostly for attribution.)
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

content.text:
**Round 2 for my 12 talks (80 entries): 35 GO, 45 FIX, 0 NO-GO, so 56% needed changes.** All 45 fixes are applied in the entry files. Nothing was deleted, committed or promoted, and the vault was not touched. Every entry passes the structural checks (frontmatter, headers, no em dashes, locators within range), and all Related links resolve, both before and after the fixes. The report is at `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\Flint\staging\review_42analytics_r4a.md`.

**NO-GOs:** none. I found no invented numbers and no near-duplicates within the book; the cross-talk pairs (the Tommy John trio and the workload/ACWR entries) each take a different angle.

**Top 3 recurring defects:**
1. **Missing baseline tags**, about 20 fixes. Interview and SportSmith quotes lacked their Explicit tag, and Inferred course lines lacked the "speaker unconfirmed" caveat. Rounds r0, r1 and r3 all flagged this, and the earlier sweep still missed it.
2. **Captions smoothed inside quotation marks**: "mirror" for the caption's "mere", "information gain" for "game", "catch up" for "ketchup". Ambiguous garbles were also settled into one reading without a marker.
3. **Voice drift**: about 15 pronouns the captions never give, and invented links between people ("same presenters", whose co-author someone is). One Q&A answer was credited to the wrong one of two presenters. Name attribution itself is now clean.

**Confidence changes:** three entries were lowered: one second-hand survey, one method-only entry and one `contested` with no real conflict.

**Unassigned:** two of the other reviewer's entries cite EeBgUCYhezc. The sentences citing it check out (GO), and I did not edit those files. `heuristic--year-to-year-stability...` cites only the other reviewer's talks, so I did not review it.

**Recommendation: needs another fix pass before promotion.** The same three defects probably run through the other 72 entries. Run a folder-wide grep for untagged baseline lines and unsupported pronouns, fix what it finds, then spot-check about 10 entries before promoting.
